title: Website Design & Development
description:
We are looking for an experienced web designer/developer or an agency to design and build a professional website for a U.S.-based company operating in a regulated industry.

The website will have approximately 10–15 pages.

Expected pages will include:

* Home
* About Us
* Products
* Technologies
* Services
* Quality
* Contact
* Privacy Policy
* Terms of Service
* Additional product/service or informational pages as needed

Project Requirements

The website should have a modern, professional design and work properly across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.

We also need:

* Approximately 10–15 total pages
* Professional UI/UX design
* Responsive/mobile-friendly development
* Easy-to-use content management system
* Ability for our staff to update text, images, products, and other website content without needing a developer
* WordPress or another user-friendly CMS can be considered
* Contact forms
* Basic SEO structure and metadata
* Proper security configuration and development best practices
* Payment gateway integration
* Stripe is preferred, but we are open to other reputable payment solutions you recommend
* SSL/HTTPS configuration
* Analytics integration
* Cookie/privacy configuration where applicable
* Proper testing before launch

Important: No Sloppy AI-Generated Work

We are not looking for a website that is simply generated by AI, copied from a generic template, or assembled quickly without proper review.

AI tools may be used as part of your normal workflow, but the final work must be professionally designed, developed, reviewed, tested, and customized for our company.

We will not accept:

* Generic AI-generated layouts with minimal customization
* AI-generated content that has not been professionally reviewed
* Placeholder or fabricated content
* Poorly structured code
* Unnecessary plugins or dependencies
* Copy-and-paste templates presented as custom work
* Broken responsive layouts
* Inconsistent styling between pages
* Poor accessibility practices
* Security shortcuts
* Code that the developer cannot explain or maintain

You should be able to explain the architecture, technology choices, security controls, integrations, and code that you deliver.

Quality is more important to us than simply completing the project quickly.

Third-Party Audit / Review

Because the company operates in a regulated industry, the completed website will be reviewed and audited by an independent third-party provider before going live.

The developer must be willing to address reasonable technical, security, accessibility, privacy, or implementation findings identified during that review before final production launch.

We are looking for someone who follows proper development practices and is comfortable having their work independently reviewed.

Documentation / SOP

Complete project documentation is required.

At the end of the project, we need a clear SOP/documentation package explaining:

* How the website is structured
* How to log in and administer the website
* How to update text/content
* How to replace or upload pictures
* How to add or modify pages
* How to update products or services
* How forms are managed
* How the payment gateway is configured and managed
* How plugins, themes, frameworks, or dependencies should be updated
* Backup and recovery procedures
* General website maintenance procedures

The documentation should be written so that a normal business user can manage common website changes without advanced technical knowledge.

Ownership and Handoff

At project completion, our company must have full ownership and administrative access to:

* Website source code
* CMS
* Domain
* Hosting
* Database
* Stripe/payment gateway account
* Analytics
* Design/source files
* Plugins and licenses purchased specifically for the project
* Third-party integrations
* Administrator accounts and credentials
* Git/source-code repository, if applicable

We do not want to be dependent on the original developer to make normal updates or maintain access to our own website.

### When Applying

Please provide:

1. Examples of websites you have personally designed and developed.
2. Your recommended platform/technology for this project and why.
3. Whether you recommend WordPress, a custom CMS, or another platform.
4. Your experience integrating Stripe or other payment gateways.
5. Your experience working on websites for regulated industries, if applicable.
6. Your approach to website security and quality assurance.
7. Your estimated completion timeline for a 10–15 page website.
8. Your **fixed-price quote for the entire project**.
9. What is included and excluded from your fixed price.
10. How many design revisions are included.
11. Whether you will address findings from our third-party audit before launch.
12. Whether complete documentation/SOP and final source files are included.
13. Who will actually perform the design and development work.
14. Whether any part of the project will be outsourced.
15. What AI tools, if any, you use in your development or design process.

We are specifically looking for a **fixed-price project**, not an open-ended hourly engagement.

Please provide a realistic price and timeline based on the scope above.

We value quality, maintainability, security, and professional craftsmanship over the fastest or cheapest proposal.

Thank you.

title: Web Developer, Revenue Share, Work How You Want
description:
We're a web development agency with a steady flow of client work, and we're looking for developers who want to own projects rather than be managed through them.

How the money works:
You get 40% of every project you complete. After platform fees that's effectively half of what actually reaches us, so we split what comes in with the person who did the work. There's no ceiling on it.

You don't sell anything. The clients are ours and the work is already coming in. What you earn depends on how much you complete well, not on how much you can bring in.

If you'd rather have some security, there are options with a monthly base and a lower share. A $200 base with 35%, $350 with 30%, or $500 with 25%. Full commission pays more from around $3,300 of completed work a month and keeps climbing from there. You pick, and you can switch each quarter.

Realistically, someone working steadily lands between $1,400 and $2,800 a month. Someone fast lands higher.

How we work:
One project, one person, start to finish. Design, build, client communication, the lot. Nobody hands you half a project and nobody waits on you to finish a piece of theirs.

No meetings. We dropped the weekly call entirely. No fixed hours either. Where you work and when is your business.

What we need instead is simple: ClickUp kept current, deadlines held, and the client happy with what they get. That's it. Everything else is yours to decide.

Platforms: WordPress, Shopify, Wix, Squarespace and GoHighLevel. You need real hands-on experience with at least two or three and the ability to pick up the rest fast. Wix, Squarespace and GoHighLevel are where we're most short right now.

How we work with AI:
AI is how most of the work gets done here. Our primary tool is Claude and Claude Code. You use it for building layouts, writing code, debugging and adapting content, and you prompt precisely enough to get usable output fast.

And you check what it produces. You read it, catch what's wrong and fix it by hand when it goes off track. That means understanding HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Liquid and PHP well enough to take over. This is the part most applicants get wrong, so be specific about how you do it.

What we need from you:
Reachable during European business hours and quick to reply. Clients are mostly European.

Deadlines held, and problems flagged early rather than at the last minute.

Fluent English. You write the client replies yourself, ready to send.

Comfort with multilingual sites. A lot of our work is German, French and Spanish. You use AI for languages you don't speak and check carefully that nothing breaks.

And the thing that matters most: you check your own work before it leaves your hands. That's what the whole arrangement rests on.

How this works:
One paid screening project in two stages. We send a brief, you come back with two genuinely different design concepts, 48 hours. We pick one and give feedback, you build it out, another 48 hours. Paid as fixed price milestones.

If that goes well, you're in.

To apply:
Start your proposal with the word GENERALIST, then answer the screening questions. Include live links to sites you've built with the platform named next to each. Applications without those won't be reviewed.

title: WordPress Developer for Gwenlightenment
description:
WordPress Developer Needed for Paid Test Page + Potential Full Gwenlightenment Website Build & Long-Term Work

PROJECT OVERVIEW

I am looking for an experienced WordPress developer/designer to potentially build the complete website for my project, Gwenlightenment.

Before hiring someone for the full website, I would like to begin with a paid test project so I can evaluate your development ability, design judgment, communication, attention to detail, responsiveness, and how well we work together.

The paid test will be the complete development of one important page: Gwenlightenment — Start Here / Landing Page

Test project budget: $100–$150 fixed price.

I will provide the page content, structure/page brief, branding direction, design references, inspiration websites, and visual mockups/references.

I am not looking for someone to simply reproduce a template or create a generic WordPress page. Gwenlightenment is intended to feel like its own immersive little world: beautiful, warm, artistic, soulful, nature-inspired, intuitive, and memorable while still being extremely easy to navigate.

The design concepts I have show the general visual direction and atmosphere I am interested in. They are inspiration rather than pixel-perfect instructions. 

I want a developer/designer who can use their own creativity and professional judgment to translate the Gwenlightenment brand into a polished, functional website.


THE PAID TEST PROJECT

The test project is to fully build the Start Here page, which will function as the primary landing/home experience visitors encounter when entering Gwenlightenment.

The page will introduce the Gwenlightenment world and direct visitors toward the different areas of the website. 

The page will include multiple navigation buttons and calls to action leading to pages that will not necessarily exist yet during the test build. Those destination pages do NOT need to be built as part of this test. However, the buttons, cards, navigation elements, hover states, interactive elements, and intended user pathways should still be created so I can evaluate how the finished page will function. Placeholder URLs such as # or another agreed method can be used until the full site is built.

For the test page, I am evaluating:
•	Overall visual quality and polish 
•	Ability to translate a creative brief into an actual website 
•	WordPress development skill 
•	Ability to create something custom rather than template-looking 
•	Layout and visual hierarchy 
•	Typography and spacing 
•	Responsive behavior 
•	Desktop, tablet, and mobile execution 
•	Navigation clarity 
•	Button/card interactions 
•	Hover effects and micro-interactions 
•	Creative use of imagery, botanical elements, textures, layering, etc. 
•	Page speed and reasonable performance 
•	Clean implementation 
•	Accessibility-conscious development 
•	Ability to create reusable systems/components 
•	Communication 
•	Ability to take and implement feedback 
•	Attention to small details 
•	Ability to preserve the artistic design without sacrificing usability 

I am open to Gutenberg, Bricks, Elementor, custom theme development, or another appropriate WordPress approach, but I would like you to explain what development stack you recommend and why.

I do not want the website dependent on an excessive number of plugins or difficult-to-maintain customizations.

WORDPRESS ACCESS + EXISTING WEBSITE PROTECTION

The Start Here test page will be developed within my existing WordPress website/account. The selected developer will be provided an appropriate WordPress user account/access level necessary to complete the agreed work.

The developer must not make destructive or unrelated changes to the existing website. This includes deleting existing content, modifying unrelated pages or settings, changing hosting/domain/account ownership, removing existing functionality, or making other changes outside the agreed scope without my prior approval.

The developer may install or configure themes, plugins, code, integrations, or other tools necessary for the agreed work only when appropriate to the project. Any premium plugin, theme, service, API, software license, subscription, or other item that would create an additional or recurring cost must be disclosed to and approved by me before purchase or installation.

Before making any significant site-wide changes during the test project, the developer should confirm that a current, restorable backup of the website exists. If a current backup does not already exist, an appropriate backup should be created before those changes are made, provided the developer has the necessary access to do so. The developer should not intentionally overwrite or remove an existing usable backup without my prior approval.

All primary WordPress, hosting, domain, plugin, service, and related website accounts should remain under my ownership and control. The developer should work through the access/account permissions I provide rather than transferring the website or its core services into developer-owned accounts.

Development access should not be shared with any other person without my permission.

The developer should not publish the Start Here page publicly on the live website, make the page the site's active homepage, or otherwise make unfinished test work publicly accessible without my approval. Development/review should remain unpublished, private, staged, or otherwise appropriately restricted until I approve it for public use.


TEST PROJECT DELIVERABLES

The test contract includes:

1. Complete Start Here page development
The full page will be built according to the page brief, content, branding, mockups, and reference material I provide.

2. Responsive development
The page must work properly across:
•	Desktop 
•	Laptop 
•	Tablet 
•	Mobile 

The mobile version should be intentionally designed rather than simply shrinking the desktop layout.

The completed page should also be checked in current major browsers, including Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge, with any significant browser-specific layout or functionality issues corrected.

3. Header/navigation
Build the intended Gwenlightenment header/navigation shown in the page brief/design direction.
Links to pages that do not yet exist may remain placeholders during the trial.

4. Footer
Build the intended footer for the page.

5. Interactive elements
Buttons, cards, menus, hover states, transitions, and other appropriate interactions should function as intended.

I am interested in tasteful custom interactions/animation where they improve the experience, but I do not want excessive animation that makes the site distracting or slow.

6. Reusable styling/components
Whenever practical, sections should be developed using reusable global styles/components rather than individually hard-coded styling that becomes difficult to maintain later.

7. Basic technical quality
The page should follow good WordPress development practices and should not create unnecessary performance, security, accessibility, or maintainability problems.

This includes reasonable accessibility fundamentals such as semantic heading structure, keyboard-accessible interactive elements, visible focus states, descriptive alternative text where applicable, appropriately labeled forms/controls where applicable, and sufficient text/background contrast.

8. Revision round
Please include at least one consolidated revision round within the trial price so I can give feedback and evaluate how we work together during revisions.

9. WordPress Development Access + Handoff
The Start Here page will be developed within my existing WordPress website/account using the access I provide.

I should be able to review the actual functioning page within WordPress throughout or upon completion of the test rather than receiving only screenshots/mockups of the proposed page.

Upon completion of the paid test, the completed page and its associated implementation should remain within my WordPress website/account. Any developer-specific access that is no longer required may be removed after the project is complete.

10. Test Page Completion Criteria
The test project will be considered complete after:
•	The full Start Here page described in the provided page brief has been implemented in WordPress. 
•	The page has been intentionally adapted for desktop, laptop, tablet, and mobile. 
•	The intended header, footer, buttons, cards, navigation elements, hover states, and applicable interactions are implemented. 
•	Placeholder links have been added where destination pages do not yet exist. 
•	There are no obvious broken layouts, major functional errors, or unintended horizontal overflow on standard screen sizes. 
•	The page is reasonably optimized for performance and images are appropriately optimized for web use. 
•	The agreed revision round has been completed. 
•	I have access to the completed implementation within my WordPress website/account.


OWNERSHIP OF TEST WORK

This is a paid test project. Once the agreed test-project payment has been completed, I should receive the completed work created under the contract and access to the implementation in accordance with Upwork's applicable contract/IP terms.

Please do not use unlicensed themes, plugins, fonts, images, graphics, scripts, or other assets. If any premium theme, plugin, stock asset, font, API, or third-party service would require an additional purchase or recurring fee, please tell me before using it.


WHAT HAPPENS AFTER THE TEST?

Completing the paid test project does not guarantee selection for the full website project.

If I decide that we are a good fit, I intend to hire the selected developer under a separate contract/milestone agreement for the complete Gwenlightenment website.

If selected:
•	The Start Here page created during this test will become part of the actual production website. 
•	The amount I paid for the test project will be credited toward the mutually agreed total price of the full website build. 
•	We will establish the complete scope, price, milestones, timeline, deliverables, revisions, and launch requirements under the new agreement. 

If I decide not to continue with you, you will still be paid the agreed amount for completing the test project, and we will simply end the project there.

If I select you for the full website project, the completed Start Here page will become part of the production website rather than being rebuilt from scratch, and the amount paid under this test contract will be credited against the mutually agreed development price of the subsequent full-site contract.


IMPORTANT: SCOPE OF THE POTENTIAL FULL WEBSITE

This contract is specifically for the development of the Gwenlightenment Start Here / Landing Page only.

The complete Gwenlightenment website will be covered under a separate contract/milestone agreement if I choose to continue working with the developer after the paid test. That future agreement will establish the final full-site scope, architecture, development price, milestones, timeline, deliverables, revisions, and launch requirements.

I am including the potential full-site scope within this job post because I want applicants to understand the size and complexity of the eventual project before accepting the paid test. I am looking for the test developer with the possibility of continuing into the complete website build, so it is important that applicants are comfortable with the type of functionality, architecture, and long-term development the full Gwenlightenment website will eventually require.

Gwenlightenment will be a large WordPress ecosystem combining:
education + spirituality + recipes + digital products + physical products + memberships + subscriptions + AI tools + local bakery ordering + community/member resources + donations + interactive libraries + email automation.

It will also operate as a private membership association website, so the eventual site will need a properly planned logged-out/logged-in experience.

Some content will remain publicly accessible.

Other pages, resources, products, downloads, and/or experiences will require visitors to:
Create a free account → log in → access the appropriate member content.

Paid memberships and subscriptions will have their own access requirements.

The eventual developer therefore needs to be comfortable architecting a website with multiple user states and content-access rules, not just building static pages.


MAJOR AREAS OF THE EVENTUAL WEBSITE

The complete site is expected to include the following types of sections and functionality.

Learn
Educational/resource areas including:

Free Education
A searchable and organized blog/library of free educational articles.

Free Clearings
A library of free spiritual clearing scripts/articles.

My Bookshelf

Recommendations & Resources

Recipes

Premium Recipes — individual recipes available for purchase.
Recipe Library Membership — a recurring monthly/yearly paid membership providing access to the free recipes, premium recipes, and additional member-exclusive recipes.

This section introduces the spiritual foundation of Gwenlightenment and its relationship to the Gaian Christos faith and Inner Flame Ministries.
Gaian Christos centers on spiritual remembrance, Christ Consciousness, Gaia, holistic healing, spiritual education, and the integration of sacred wisdom and lived practice. Its sacred writings similarly describe the Inner Flame and the relationship between humanity, Gaia, divine consciousness, remembrance, sovereignty, and spiritual practice. 
Most pages within this area will be informational.
The Sacred Writings area will additionally connect visitors with downloadable books/products and the separate Inner Flame Ministries/Gaian Christos website.

This is my local bakery/food project.

This Week's Menu — a changing weekly catalog/menu that needs to be extremely easy for us to update ourselves.
Order for Pickup — local e-commerce/checkout for customers ordering baked goods for pickup in the San Antonio/New Braunfels, Texas area.

Apothecary

Gwenlightenment AI Tools

Take Action

It will include petition-related content, links to outside petition initiatives, Gwenlightenment petition forms, and ways to support the mission.

Help the Mission Grow

About Gwen

There will also eventually be a playful Future Husband Application page containing a compatibility/application form and optional contribution/donation functionality.

Membership

The full site will require:

Help / Support

ESTIMATED LAUNCH CONTENT

EMAIL + AUTOMATION REQUIREMENTS FOR THE EVENTUAL WEBSITE

BASIC SEO + SEARCH ENGINE SETUP FOR WEBSITE LAUNCH

I understand that no developer or SEO provider can guarantee specific Google rankings. title: Website building
description:
We are looking for an experienced website designer/developer to build a professional, modern, and easy-to-manage website for our local dance/fitness studio and event rental space.

We are NOT necessarily looking for a completely custom-coded website. We are open to using an established platform and integrations if that will give us the functionality we need while keeping the website affordable, secure, and easy for us to maintain ourselves.

Our goal is to create one central website that serves our clients, instructors, and event-rental customers.

WEBSITE FEATURES

• Professional, modern, mobile-friendly website

• Studio information, photos, location, FAQs, reviews/testimonials, instructor information, etc.

• Live class calendar that can easily be updated as classes are added, changed, or canceled

• Clients should be able to view classes and sign up/register

• Individual class listings should include information such as instructor, date/time, class description, price, availability, and registration/payment link

INSTRUCTOR ACCOUNTS & CLASS MANAGEMENT

We would ideally like instructors to have individual accounts with limited permissions.

Instructors should be able to:

• Log into their own account

• Add and manage their own classes

• Update class descriptions, dates, times, pricing, etc.

• Add their own registration/payment link

• Access studio policies, agreements, forms, and resources

Instructors should NOT have access to other instructors’ private information or the overall administrative side of the website.

PAYMENTS

We specifically do NOT want our business collecting class fees on behalf of individual instructors.

Each instructor should be able to connect or provide their own outside registration/payment link so their class payments go directly to them.

The studio does need the ability to collect payments that belong directly to the studio, such as:

• Instructor studio rental fees

• Event rental fees/deposits if we decide to accept those online

These payments should go directly to our business payment processor/account.

INSTRUCTOR ONBOARDING & DOCUMENT MANAGEMENT

We would like an instructor onboarding system or portal that allows us to send a new instructor one link and have them complete the required onboarding process.

This should ideally include:

• Electronic instructor agreements/contracts

• Electronic liability waiver

• Studio policies/forms

• Proof/certificate of insurance upload

• Certification/CPR or other credential uploads when applicable

• Other required instructor documentation

If sensitive identification documents are ever required, such as a driver’s license, we do NOT want these stored in a standard website media/file library. We would want a secure document-management solution with appropriate encryption, access controls, and privacy protections.

We would like an administrative dashboard or similar system where we can quickly see each instructor’s onboarding status, for example:

Agreement – Complete
Liability Waiver – Complete
Insurance – Complete
CPR/Certification – Complete

It would also be very helpful to track expiration dates for insurance, CPR, certifications, etc. and receive reminders when updated documentation is needed.

CLIENT LIABILITY WAIVERS

We would like clients/participants to be able to electronically sign our studio liability waiver.

The system should maintain a record of completed waivers so we can verify whether someone has a current waiver on file.

Because we offer children’s classes, we also need an appropriate process for a parent/legal guardian to sign on behalf of a minor.

EVENT RENTAL SECTION

Our studio is also available as an event rental venue.

We would like a separate section of the website dedicated to event rentals that can include:

• Photos of the space

• Amenities

• Rental information and/or pricing

• FAQs

• Contact Us / Request More Information form

• Potential availability/inquiry functionality

• Electronic event rental agreement and waiver, if appropriate

ADMINISTRATIVE REQUIREMENTS

One of our biggest priorities is ease of use after the website is completed.

We need to be able to manage normal day-to-day updates ourselves without contacting a developer every time something changes.

Owners/admins should be able to easily:

• Add/edit/remove classes

• Add/remove instructors

• Update schedules

• Update photos and website content

• Change pricing/information

• Review registrations when applicable

• Review instructor onboarding/document status

• Review signed waivers

• Manage event rental information

The website must work extremely well on mobile devices since we expect many customers to access it from their phones.

WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU

When submitting your proposal, please include:

1. Examples of similar websites you have built, especially dance studios, fitness studios, yoga/Pilates studios, class-based businesses, membership systems, or event venues.
2. The platform you recommend for this project and WHY you recommend it.
3. How you would build the live class calendar and registration system.
4. How you would allow instructors to manage their own classes without giving them full website access.
5. How you would structure payments so individual instructors receive their class payments directly while the studio separately receives its rental/event payments.
6. What system you recommend for electronic contracts and liability waivers.
7. How you recommend handling secure instructor document uploads and storage.
8. Whether/how the system can track expiration dates for insurance and certifications.
9. Your estimated timeline from start to launch.
10. Your estimated TOTAL project cost.
11. A breakdown of any ongoing expenses we should expect, including hosting, software, scheduling/booking systems, payment processing, e-signatures, document storage, plugins, or other monthly/annual fees.
12. What ongoing maintenance, if any, you believe would require a developer after launch.

We are looking for someone who can recommend the RIGHT solution rather than automatically building everything from scratch.

The finished website should be professional and polished for our customers while being simple and practical for us to operate behind the scenes.

Please begin your proposal by telling us which platform/system you would recommend for this project and why. This will help us identify applicants who have reviewed the full project requirements

ABOUT US
Duraamen Engineered Products manufactures and supplies specialty flooring systems — microcement, urethane concrete, epoxy and polished-concrete products — sold to contractors and specifiers across the United States and the GCC. We run nine WordPress installs: a primary corporate site with a WooCommerce store, five regional market sites, a UAE site, a separate microcement brand, and a contractor directory. Hosting is WP Engine, fronted by Cloudflare.

WHAT WE HAVE ALREADY DONE
In September 2026 we commissioned an independent crawl of every URL in every sitemap across the estate — 2,160 pages — and recorded 9,177 defects itemised per URL with severity. We then reconciled 12,279 historically archived URLs against the current sitemaps and re-tested the critical findings live. You are not being asked to discover the problems. They are documented, with URLs, in the attached work package.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG (all verified)
•	Zero of 204 WooCommerce shop, product and product-category URLs carry Product schema. No Product, no Offer, no AggregateRating — while Google Listings & Ads and Facebook for WooCommerce are both installed and active.
•	A contractor-directory template returns a live, indexable HTTP 200 page for any arbitrary string in one URL segment. An unbounded crawl trap. Its canonical output is cache-variant: the same URL returns a broken template token, no canonical, or the correct value on different requests.
•	Roughly 1,600 historical URLs return 404 with no redirect. Four site rebuilds since 2009 and no redirect map was ever built. The affected set includes article URLs from 2019 through 2025, not just old ones.
•	433 pages have no H1 element. 759 have more than one, some with 15 to 17. Verified identical across browser, Googlebot and neutral user agents, so this is template-level, not a rendering artefact.
•	74 internal links on live pages point at hard 404s. A further 747 point at redirecting URLs. 753 point at WordPress attachment pages.
•	1,107 pages have no meta description. 9,714 images have no alt attribute. The primary site serves 43 WebP images out of 20,580.
•	Two regional sites carry no LocalBusiness schema at all — they are typed as Article with a Person author.
•	The primary site's homepage loads 79 CSS files and 97 JS files, 5.36 MB across 178 requests, with no page-caching plugin and Cloudflare bypassing HTML. It also runs two Advanced Coupons builds, three freight-quote plugins and two cookie-consent plugins simultaneously.
•	One WordPress install on our primary domain has been unmaintained since 2023 and is fully indexable. We treat that as a security finding first.
THE WORK, IN THREE MILESTONES
Milestone 1 — Day 1 to 15. Verified backups and staging clones for every site with a tested rollback path. Baseline capture from Search Console and analytics, signed off before anything changes. Then indexation integrity: kill the crawl trap at the rewrite-rule level, make canonical output deterministic against a purged cache, clean the sitemaps, remove stale and competing sitemap files, remove Crawl-delay directives, resolve origin instability.
Milestone 2 — Day 16 to 30. Product and Offer schema across all 204 commercial URLs at template level. Complete per-market LocalBusiness markup. Fix the H1 defects in the theme templates, not page by page. Metadata remediation at volume. Decide and implement the handling of 214 near-duplicate product-tag archives. Reciprocal hreflang with x-default.
Milestone 3 — Day 31 to 45. Deploy the 301 redirect map for the dead historical URLs, no chains, no blanket homepage redirects. Repair the internal link defects. Image alt and WebP programme. Front-end payload, caching and Core Web Vitals to a pass on mobile. Then a full re-crawl and a Search Console comparison against the Day-1 baseline.

HOW WE WORK — NON-NEGOTIABLE
•	Nothing touches production without a verified backup, a staging test and a post-deploy smoke test.
•	Every change is logged: date, site, component, version, staging result, production result, rollback status.
•	No task is complete on assertion. It is complete when it is live, re-tested, and evidenced with URLs, crawl output and Search Console data.
•	No purchased links, no auto-translated content, no placeholder or duplicated location-template copy.

title: Senior WooCommerce + Google Merchant Center Developer Needed – GLA / Sale Price Sync Debugging
description:
We are looking for a senior WooCommerce developer with genuine hands-on experience debugging Google Merchant Center / Google for WooCommerce (formerly Google Listings & Ads) product-price synchronisation issues.

This is not a Google Ads management, SEO, basic Merchant Center setup, or general WordPress job.

I specifically need someone who understands the technical path between:

WooCommerce product pricing
Google for WooCommerce / Google Listings & Ads (GLA)
Google Merchant Center
Content API / Merchant API
WordPress Action Scheduler / WP-Cron
WooCommerce price hooks/filters
Custom pricing/API integrations
PHP-level debugging

I already have an experienced WooCommerce developer investigating the issue. His work has been excellent and he is actively working on it.

However, because this pricing problem is currently affecting our Google Shopping advertising and ability to generate sales, I would like a second experienced pair of eyes with specific WooCommerce → Google Merchant Center integration experience.

The initial engagement will be diagnosis/review only.

I do not want two developers simultaneously making changes to the production website. I want an independent technical assessment first.

If your investigation identifies the cause and we agree on the solution, I would be happy to extend the contract to implementation and potentially ongoing/long-term WooCommerce development work.

Current problem

We operate a WooCommerce store with approximately 130 products and a custom pricing setup that uses Amazon pricing data as part of calculating our selling prices.

WooCommerce and the customer-facing website can currently contain the correct customer-facing prices.

However, we are experiencing an intermittent issue where Google Merchant Center receives the regular price correctly but loses or fails to receive the WooCommerce sale_price for some products.

For example, one product should contain:

Regular price: £238.68
Sale/customer-facing price: £187.99

Following certain synchronisations, Merchant Center correctly receives both values:

price = £238.68
sale_price = £187.99

However, later the sale_price can disappear from Merchant Center, leaving only the £238.68 regular price.

Google Shopping/Ads can therefore advertise the wrong price even though the website itself is displaying the correct customer-facing price.

This behaviour is inconsistent across the catalogue.

At one point, approximately 35–40% of products had the correct sale price populated in Merchant Center while the remainder did not.

We have also observed an important pattern:

Products can become correct following one scheduled synchronisation and subsequently become incorrect again.

Relevant history – WooCommerce performance work

There is important background that may or may not be related.

Earlier this year, our existing developer carried out a detailed WooCommerce performance audit of the website.

The audit identified significant backend activity, including unusually heavy scheduled/background processing associated with Google Listings & Ads / Google for WooCommerce.

Following the audit, several performance/backend changes were implemented to improve the reliability and performance of the website.

This included work relating to areas such as:

WordPress/WooCommerce scheduled jobs
Action Scheduler / cron behaviour
Google for WooCommerce synchronisation activity
Caching/performance
Database/query performance
Other WooCommerce backend optimisation

The performance work itself successfully improved the website.

I want to make clear that I am not claiming these changes caused the subsequent pricing problems.

However, the chronology is relevant because I was not experiencing these recurring pricing/synchronisation problems before this period of backend work.

I therefore want the relationship, if any, independently investigated rather than assumed.

First pricing problem – WooCommerce prices dropping approximately 20%

After the performance/backend work, we began experiencing a recurring WooCommerce pricing issue.

Approximately every 3–4 days, virtually all of our in-stock products would suddenly drop in price by roughly 20%.

Our external Amazon pricing system/database still contained the correct calculated prices, but the prices actually stored/displayed by WooCommerce became incorrect.

Importantly, manually rerunning our price-sync jobs would immediately restore the correct WooCommerce prices.

Our existing developer investigated this and was able to reproduce the behaviour on staging.

The investigation initially identified behaviour involving the Import Products from Amazon plugin.

Further investigation indicated that there appeared to be a loop/interference between our Amazon pricing synchronisation and an older discount/pricing plugin.

During certain price reads, the discount logic appeared capable of returning a figure approximately 20% too low. The synchronisation process could then save that value back into WooCommerce.

This explained why:

many products changed at approximately the same time;
the change was approximately the same percentage;
our external pricing system still contained the correct values; and
manually rerunning the price synchronisation immediately corrected WooCommerce.

Changes were subsequently made to prevent the discount logic from affecting those price reads.

The recurring ~20% WooCommerce price-drop problem now appears to have been resolved.

What happened afterwards – Google Merchant Center mismatch

After the WooCommerce pricing problem was corrected, we subsequently began experiencing the current Google Merchant Center pricing problem.

The distinction is important:

Previously, WooCommerce itself was receiving/storing incorrect prices.

Now, WooCommerce and the customer-facing website can have the correct price, while Google Merchant Center receives a different representation of the product.

In particular, Merchant Center may receive the regular price but fail to retain/receive sale_price.

For some products, a scheduled sync restores the correct sale_price.

Later, something appears capable of causing that sale price to disappear again.

What our existing developer has found so far

Our current developer has confirmed that scheduled feed synchronisation is capable of producing the correct sale prices.

For example, he verified products where Merchant Center correctly received the expected customer-facing sale_price.

However, something subsequently appears capable of stripping, omitting or failing to supply sale_price for certain products.

His current working theory is that Google may be obtaining product data from the website/WooCommerce through another channel or synchronisation path that isn't seeing the discount/sale price correctly, triggering later updates with different pricing data.

He has now added logging intended to identify which channel/process is responsible.

I do not want applicants simply to accept this theory.

I want an independent senior developer to review the evidence and architecture and reach their own technical conclusion.

Why I am providing the full history

The chronology currently looks roughly like this:

WooCommerce performance/backend optimisation

→ Recurring ~20% WooCommerce pricing problem

→ Pricing-read/discount interaction identified and changed

→ WooCommerce pricing stabilised

What the site cannot do is talk to a server, because it is static. We need it implemented on WordPress and eleven specific things made functional. The full list is below and in the attached spec.

We host with Bluehost on WordPress. Stripe is our only payment processor and will stay that way — please do not propose PayPal, Square or an alternative gateway.

What needs to be built

Implement the 18 pages on WordPress — preserving layout, type, spacing and colors exactly, and keeping the existing JobPosting, FAQPage, Service and Product schema intact. The site was built for search and answer-engine visibility and we do not want that lost.
A WooCommerce cart — 27 products: 2 subscriptions, 4 services, 6 digital templates, 14 merchandise items, 1 free download. Products already exist in our Stripe account; reuse them. Today each item links to its own Stripe Payment Link and buyers cannot combine items.
Recurring billing for two subscriptions — $4.99/month membership and $1,999/month retainer. Core WooCommerce does not do this; tell us in your proposal how you would handle it and what it costs.
Stripe customer portal enabled — so subscribers cancel and update cards themselves instead of emailing us.
Automatic digital delivery — six paid templates plus one free download. We supply the files; buyers should receive them on payment without us touching anything.
Correct tax codes by product type — everything currently carries one physical-goods code, which is wrong for services, digital goods and the membership.
Seven forms wired up — consult request, job application with resume upload, newsletter signup, and four lead-magnet email captures. All seven currently validate and confirm on screen, then discard the data.
Four lead magnets delivered by autoresponder — a resume audit, a California compliance checklist, an exempt vs. non-exempt quick check and a free store download. Each promises a PDF by email. We supply the files.
Newsletter connected to a mail service — Mailchimp, Kit or Brevo, with double opt-in and unsubscribe. Our privacy policy already commits to this.
A scheduler on the contact page — Calendly, Cal.com or similar. The FAQ tells clients sessions are booked on a booking link and none exists yet.
Membership access gated — paying $4.99 currently grants nothing enforced. We plan to share a Google Drive folder; tell us whether you would gate it in WordPress instead, and how cancellations would revoke access.
Also carry over intact

Dark mode toggle with persistence. Header dropdown menus and mobile drawer. On-site search over page content and page sections. Two SociableKit feed widgets (HR news RSS and Instagram), one styled into a narrow homepage sidebar. A retention rule on job application data — our privacy policy commits to deleting resumes after twelve months. And pick one source for sitemap.xml and robots.txt; we have static files at the root and an SEO plugin would generate its own.

Launch checks before handover

SSL, admin 2FA, a backup routine, Google Search Console verified and the sitemap submitted, and test purchases run across all four product types.

What you get from us

All 18 pages and the shared header and footer as finished HTML with assets. A written spec covering the full product list, categories, shipping rule, tax codes and delivery settings. Stripe and Bluehost access. Direct access to the owner for decisions, usually same-day.

Required experience

Proven WooCommerce builds with the Stripe gateway — please link two live stores you have built
Recurring billing or subscription commerce
Implementing supplied designs faithfully rather than substituting a theme
Digital-product delivery and tax configuration
Clear written English and a predictable weekly update
Nice to have

Professional services or consulting clients. Technical SEO: schema preservation, Core Web Vitals, Search Console. Accessibility (WCAG AA) awareness.

How we would like to run it

We would prefer to work in four milestones rather than one lump contract, so both sides can see progress early:

Port three pages — Home, Store and Contact — proving the design and schema carry over faithfully
The remaining 15 pages, plus dark mode, navigation, search and the feed widgets
WooCommerce with all 27 products, shipping and physical merchandise
Subscriptions, digital delivery, tax codes and the membership gate
Propose a price per milestone. If you would rather structure it differently, tell us why.

Project details

One project, roughly 3–4 weeks. Fixed-price per milestone preferred. Start immediately. We are reviewing several proposals and will pick on demonstrated WooCommerce and Stripe experience rather than on price alone.

In your proposal, please answer

Two live WooCommerce stores you built, with the Stripe integration visible
How you would handle the two recurring subscriptions, and what it costs
Your approach to implementing supplied HTML on WordPress — page builder, custom theme or block templates, and why
Your total fixed price and the milestones
What you need from us before you can start
Please do not send a generic proposal. Reference something specific from this post so we know you read it.
